query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled amount of aluminum into a refractory HEA (e.g., NbMoTaW) will promote the in situ formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure in an oxygen‐rich environment, thereby significantly reducing the oxidation rate relative to the untreated alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: A refractory high-entropy alloy such as NbMoTaW with its baseline composition (no excess aluminum) and no preformed protective oxide layer.
generation.intervention: Bulk alloying (or surface enrichment) with roughly 5 at.% aluminum to allow for preferential oxidation of Al at high temperature.
generation.conditions: Exposure at around 900 °C in air (or an oxygen-containing atmosphere at approximately 0.21 atm O2) for an extended duration (e.g., 100 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Aluminum has a high affinity for oxygen, and when present in the alloy, it oxidizes preferentially to form an Al2O3 layer. This oxide has a low oxygen diffusivity and acts as a barrier, reducing further oxygen ingress and slowing the oxidation of the underlying alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated alloy, the Al-doped alloy will exhibit a significantly lower oxidation rate as evidenced by reduced weight gain and thinner, more protective oxide scale formation during high-temperature exposure.
generation.baseline: The untreated refractory HEA (e.g., NbMoTaW) tested under the same high-temperature oxygen-exposure conditions.
generation.boundary: This protective effect is expected to be significant under high-temperature (≈900 °C) air-exposure conditions but may not hold at temperatures where the oxide scale spalls or if the aluminum concentration is too low to form a continuous film.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal aluminum concentration, uniformity of Al distribution, and long-term adhesion of the Al2O3 scale under cyclic temperature conditions remain to be determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the baseline NbMoTaW alloy and one set with ~5 at.% aluminum addition. Expose both sets to 900 °C in air for 100 hours under identical conditions. After exposure, analyze mass change, examine surface morphology, and characterize the oxide scales using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
measurements: Thermogravimetric weight gain measurement during the exposure
Oxide scale thickness and continuity (via SEM/EDS)
Phase identification and crystallinity of the oxide (via XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction (e.g., ≥10% lower weight gain) in oxidation or do not show a well-defined, continuous Al2O3 scale compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract A novel metal matrix composite based on the NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) was designed by the in-situ formation method. The microstructure, phase evolution, and compression mechanical properties at room temperature of the composite are investigated in detail. The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina. With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA. In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material. Keywords: high entropy alloys, metal matrix composites, mechanical properties
